lines.text: An online cart holds two items at twenty dollars each.
lines.caption: An online cart holds two items at twenty dollars each.

lines.text: The subtotal is forty dollars, tax at ten percent is four, and the total is forty-four.
lines.caption: The subtotal is forty dollars, tax at ten percent is four, and the total is forty-four.

lines.text: In ordinary code, the total is computed once.
lines.caption: In ordinary code, the total is computed once.

lines.text: If the customer changes the quantity to three, the total still says forty-four, until some piece of code remembers to compute it again.
lines.caption: If the customer changes the quantity to three, the total still says forty-four, until some piece of code remembers to compute it again.

lines.text: In a spreadsheet, you never have to remember.
lines.caption: In a spreadsheet, you never have to remember.

lines.text: Change the quantity, and the subtotal, the tax and the total all update, correctly, every time.
lines.caption: Change the quantity, and the subtotal, the tax and the total all update, correctly, every time.

lines.text: Build tools do the same with files: change one source file, and exactly the parts that depend on it are rebuilt.
lines.caption: Build tools do the same with files: change one source file, and exactly the parts that depend on it are rebuilt.

lines.text: So do many U I frameworks: change a value, and the screen updates.
lines.caption: So do many UI frameworks: change a value, and the screen updates.

lines.text: How does a system like that decide what to recompute, and in what order?
lines.caption: How does a system like that decide what to recompute, and in what order?

lines.text: And what goes wrong when it gets that wrong?
lines.caption: And what goes wrong when it gets that wrong?

lines.text: Say the shop gives free shipping from sixty-five dollars.
lines.caption: Say the shop gives free shipping from sixty-five dollars.

lines.text: Each formula reads some other values.
lines.caption: Each formula reads some other values.

lines.text: The subtotal reads the price and the quantity.
lines.caption: The subtotal reads the price and the quantity.

lines.text: The tax reads the subtotal.
lines.caption: The tax reads the subtotal.

lines.text: The total reads the subtotal and the tax.
lines.caption: The total reads the subtotal and the tax.

lines.text: Free shipping reads the total, and the banner at the top of the cart reads free shipping.
lines.caption: Free shipping reads the total, and the banner at the top of the cart reads free shipping.

lines.text: Draw an arrow from each value to every formula that reads it, and you have a dependency graph.
lines.caption: Draw an arrow from each value to every formula that reads it, and you have a dependency graph.

lines.text: When the quantity changes, follow the arrows.
lines.caption: When the quantity changes, follow the arrows.

lines.text: Everything you can reach is now out of date: the subtotal, the tax, the total, free shipping, the banner.
lines.caption: Everything you can reach is now out of date: the subtotal, the tax, the total, free shipping, the banner.

lines.text: Everything you can't reach is still correct.
lines.caption: Everything you can't reach is still correct.

lines.text: The price didn't change, and nothing it feeds needs recomputing because of this edit.
lines.caption: The price didn't change, and nothing it feeds needs recomputing because of this edit.

lines.text: The obvious way to update them is to let each value tell its readers.
lines.caption: The obvious way to update them is to let each value tell its readers.

lines.text: When the quantity changes, it tells the subtotal to recompute.
lines.caption: When the quantity changes, it tells the subtotal to recompute.

lines.text: The subtotal then tells each of its own readers, and so on down the arrows.
lines.caption: The subtotal then tells each of its own readers, and so on down the arrows.

lines.text: This is the observer pattern, and it's how a lot of hand-written code keeps things in sync.
lines.caption: This is the observer pattern, and it's how a lot of hand-written code keeps things in sync.

lines.text: Follow it.
lines.caption: Follow it.

lines.text: The quantity becomes three, and the subtotal becomes sixty.
lines.caption: The quantity becomes three, and the subtotal becomes sixty.

lines.text: The subtotal has two readers, the tax and the total.
lines.caption: The subtotal has two readers, the tax and the total.

lines.text: Which does it tell first?
lines.caption: Which does it tell first?

lines.text: Whichever subscribed first; nothing in the pattern decides.
lines.caption: Whichever subscribed first; nothing in the pattern decides.

lines.text: Say it's the total.
lines.caption: Say it's the total.

lines.text: The total adds the new subtotal, sixty, to the tax, which is still the old four.
lines.caption: The total adds the new subtotal, sixty, to the tax, which is still the old four.

lines.text: The total becomes sixty-four.
lines.caption: The total becomes sixty-four.

lines.text: Sixty-four was never a correct total.
lines.caption: Sixty-four was never a correct total.

lines.text: The right answer was forty-four before the change and sixty-six after it.
lines.caption: The right answer was forty-four before the change and sixty-six after it.

lines.text: And the free-shipping check runs on sixty-four, and says no, though the right answer is yes.
lines.caption: And the free-shipping check runs on sixty-four, and says no, though the right answer is yes.

lines.text: A value like that, built from a mix of new and old inputs, is called a glitch.
lines.caption: A value like that, built from a mix of new and old inputs, is called a glitch.

lines.text: Then the subtotal tells the tax, which becomes six.
lines.caption: Then the subtotal tells the tax, which becomes six.

lines.text: The tax tells the total, which is computed again: sixty-six.
lines.caption: The tax tells the total, which is computed again: sixty-six.

lines.text: Free shipping runs a second time too.
lines.caption: Free shipping runs a second time too.

lines.text: The trouble comes from one shape.
lines.caption: The trouble comes from one shape.

lines.text: The subtotal reaches the total by two paths, directly and through the tax.
lines.caption: The subtotal reaches the total by two paths, directly and through the tax.

lines.text: A shape like that is called a diamond.
lines.caption: A shape like that is called a diamond.

lines.text: A spreadsheet or a user interface can contain many diamonds, and when they chain one after another, the cost compounds.
lines.caption: A spreadsheet or a user interface can contain many diamonds, and when they chain one after another, the cost compounds.

lines.text: In the observer pattern, each diamond makes everything after it run twice.
lines.caption: In the observer pattern, each diamond makes everything after it run twice.

lines.text: Two diamonds in a row make the last value run four times.
lines.caption: Two diamonds in a row make the last value run four times.

lines.text: Three make it eight.
lines.caption: Three make it eight.

lines.text: With ten diamonds in a row, a single change recomputes the last value one thousand and twenty-four times.
lines.caption: With ten diamonds in a row, a single change recomputes the last value one thousand and twenty-four times.

lines.text: With twenty, over a million.
lines.caption: With twenty, over a million.

lines.text: Recomputing everything in the right order would compute each value exactly once.
lines.caption: Recomputing everything in the right order would compute each value exactly once.

lines.text: So the fix works in two phases.
lines.caption: So the fix works in two phases.

lines.text: First, mark.
lines.caption: First, mark.

lines.text: Follow the arrows from the change, and mark everything reachable as out of date.
lines.caption: Follow the arrows from the change, and mark everything reachable as out of date.

lines.text: Nothing is computed yet.
lines.caption: Nothing is computed yet.

lines.text: Then compute, in order.
lines.caption: Then compute, in order.

lines.text: To get the order, give each value a height.
lines.caption: To get the order, give each value a height.

lines.text: The price and the quantity are inputs: height zero.
lines.caption: The price and the quantity are inputs: height zero.

lines.text: The subtotal reads only inputs: height one.
lines.caption: The subtotal reads only inputs: height one.

lines.text: The tax reads the subtotal: height two.
lines.caption: The tax reads the subtotal: height two.

lines.text: The total reads the tax, so it sits above it: height three.
lines.caption: The total reads the tax, so it sits above it: height three.

lines.text: Free shipping is four, and the banner five.
lines.caption: Free shipping is four, and the banner five.

lines.text: The rule: a value's height is one more than the highest height it reads.
lines.caption: The rule: a value's height is one more than the highest height it reads.

lines.text: Recompute only the marked values, from the lowest height up.
lines.caption: Recompute only the marked values, from the lowest height up.

lines.text: By the time a value is computed, every one of its inputs is already up to date.
lines.caption: By the time a value is computed, every one of its inputs is already up to date.

lines.text: The total waits until the tax is six, and becomes sixty-six the first time.
lines.caption: The total waits until the tax is six, and becomes sixty-six the first time.

lines.text: There's no sixty-four, and each value is computed once: five recomputations instead of eight.
lines.caption: There's no sixty-four, and each value is computed once: five recomputations instead of eight.

lines.text: On the chain of ten diamonds, the last value runs once instead of a thousand and twenty-four times.
lines.caption: On the chain of ten diamonds, the last value runs once instead of a thousand and twenty-four times.

lines.text: Spreadsheets, build tools and reactive libraries all use some version of this: dependencies first, each value once.
lines.caption: Spreadsheets, build tools and reactive libraries all use some version of this: dependencies first, each value once.

lines.text: And the free-shipping check runs once, on sixty-six, and says yes.
lines.caption: And the free-shipping check runs once, on sixty-six, and says yes.

lines.text: The ordered wave still recomputes everything downstream, even a value that comes out the same, and even a value nobody is looking at.
lines.caption: The ordered wave still recomputes everything downstream, even a value that comes out the same, and even a value nobody is looking at.

lines.text: Two refinements cut that out.
lines.caption: Two refinements cut that out.

lines.text: The first is early cutoff.
lines.caption: The first is early cutoff.

lines.text: Change the quantity again, from three to four.
lines.caption: Change the quantity again, from three to four.

lines.text: The subtotal, the tax and the total all change: eighty, eight, eighty-eight.
lines.caption: The subtotal, the tax and the total all change: eighty, eight, eighty-eight.

lines.text: Free shipping is recomputed, and it's still yes.
lines.caption: Free shipping is recomputed, and it's still yes.

lines.text: It didn't change, so nothing that reads it needs to run.
lines.caption: It didn't change, so nothing that reads it needs to run.

lines.text: The wave stops there.
lines.caption: The wave stops there.

lines.text: The second is laziness.
lines.caption: The second is laziness.

lines.text: A value nobody is looking at doesn't need to be computed yet.
lines.caption: A value nobody is looking at doesn't need to be computed yet.

lines.text: The system marks it as out of date, and computes it only when something reads it.
lines.caption: The system marks it as out of date, and computes it only when something reads it.

segments.title: Where do the arrows come from?

lines.text: All of this depends on the graph being right.
lines.caption: All of this depends on the graph being right.

lines.text: So where do the arrows come from?
lines.caption: So where do the arrows come from?

lines.text: Some formulas read different values depending on the data.
lines.caption: Some formulas read different values depending on the data.

lines.text: Imagine a different cart, whose total reads a coupon cell only when the customer has a coupon.
lines.caption: Imagine a different cart, whose total reads a coupon cell only when the customer has a coupon.

lines.text: There, the arrows change as the values change.
lines.caption: There, the arrows change as the values change.

lines.text: Spreadsheets and modern U I frameworks handle this by recording what each formula actually read, every time it runs.
lines.caption: Spreadsheets and modern UI frameworks handle this by recording what each formula actually read, every time it runs.

lines.text: The graph, and the heights with it, are always the ones from the last run.
lines.caption: The graph, and the heights with it, are always the ones from the last run.

lines.text: Make, the classic build tool, takes the other route.
lines.caption: Make, the classic build tool, takes the other route.

lines.text: You list, in a file called a make file, what each output is built from, unless you set up the compiler to write that list for you.
lines.caption: You list, in a file called a Makefile, what each output is built from, unless you set up the compiler to write that list for you.

lines.text: If one is missing, the graph is wrong, and the result goes stale.
lines.caption: If one is missing, the graph is wrong, and the result goes stale.

lines.text: Here's a program built from a source file that includes a header, whose make file lists only the source file.
lines.caption: Here's a program built from a source file that includes a header, whose Makefile lists only the source file.

lines.text: Change the free-shipping threshold in the header from sixty-five to seventy-five, and run make.
lines.caption: Change the free-shipping threshold in the header from sixty-five to seventy-five, and run make.

lines.text: Make says the program is up to date, and it still says sixty-five.
lines.caption: Make says the program is up to date, and it still says sixty-five.

lines.text: Declare the header, and make rebuilds it.
lines.caption: Declare the header, and make rebuilds it.

lines.text: And one kind of graph can't be ordered at all.
lines.caption: And one kind of graph can't be ordered at all.

lines.text: If a formula depends, through others, on itself, no value can come first.
lines.caption: If a formula depends, through others, on itself, no value can come first.

lines.text: Excel calls this a circular reference.
lines.caption: Excel calls this a circular reference.

lines.text: By default it warns instead of computing, though it can be told to iterate toward an answer.
lines.caption: By default it warns instead of computing, though it can be told to iterate toward an answer.

lines.text: So what does the spreadsheet know that your code doesn't?
lines.caption: So what does the spreadsheet know that your code doesn't?

lines.text: It knows the dependency graph.
lines.caption: It knows the dependency graph.

lines.text: From that graph it answers two questions: what is out of date after a change, and in what order to recompute it.
lines.caption: From that graph it answers two questions: what is out of date after a change, and in what order to recompute it.

lines.text: The answer to the first is everything downstream of the change, and nothing else.
lines.caption: The answer to the first is everything downstream of the change, and nothing else.

lines.text: The answer to the second is height order, lowest first, each value once, stopping where nothing changed.
lines.caption: The answer to the second is height order, lowest first, each value once, stopping where nothing changed.

lines.text: Get the order wrong, and you'll see values that never should exist, like a total of sixty-four.
lines.caption: Get the order wrong, and you'll see values that never should exist, like a total of sixty-four.

lines.text: And you'll do the same work many times over.
lines.caption: And you'll do the same work many times over.

lines.text: That same machine is inside Excel, inside build systems like Make and Bazel, and inside the reactive parts of U I frameworks such as View, Solid and Angular's signals.
lines.caption: That same machine is inside Excel, inside build systems like Make and Bazel, and inside the reactive parts of UI frameworks such as Vue, Solid and Angular's signals.
